performance_table.title: Performance table — August 2026 vs. prior two months

charts.title: Views & reach per day, Jun–Aug 2026
charts.takeaway: Views and reach fell together (both -7.9%/day from July to August) while the views-per-reach ratio held constant at ~1.43 — the decline is a reach/distribution issue, not a drop in content quality. [[See performance table|perf-table]]

charts.title: Interactions & link clicks per day, Jun–Aug 2026
charts.takeaway: Interactions held up far better than views (-1.3%/day vs. -7.9%/day), which is why August's engagement rate is the best of the three months. [[See engagement rate vs. benchmark|chart-benchmark]]

charts.title: Engagement rate vs. Facebook benchmark, August 2026
charts.takeaway: This account's reach-based rate (1.96%) isn't comparable to Rival IQ's 0.15% follower-based default — the export has no total-follower count to compute a like-for-like rate. [[See performance table|perf-table]]

charts.title: Revenue by content segment, August 2026
charts.takeaway: Reels generated 44% of August revenue from just 33% of views — the highest revenue-per-view of any segment. [[See segment breakdown|segment-table]]

charts.title: Daily interactions, August 2026
charts.takeaway: August 16 alone produced 9,106 interactions (66% above the month's daily average of 5,484); August 8 was the quietest day at 3,365. [[See performance table|perf-table]]

findings: Reach and views both fell 7.9%/day from July to August, but interactions dipped only 1.3%/day, pushing the reach-based engagement rate to 1.96% — the best of the three months [[Views & reach trend|chart-views-reach]], [[Performance table|perf-table]].

Reels drove a disproportionate share of monetization: 33% of August views but 44% of interactions and 44% of revenue, versus Photos' 50% of views for 47% of revenue [[Segment breakdown|segment-table]], [[Revenue by segment|chart-segment-rev]].
A single day, August 16, produced 5.4% of the month's total interactions on its own — 66% above the daily average [[Daily interactions|chart-daily-int]].
Net new followers softened to 3,708 (119.6/day) from July's 3,769 (121.6/day); the drop is fully attributable to fewer gross follows, not more unfollows [[Performance table|perf-table]].

August's 1.96% reach-based engagement rate cannot be benchmarked against Facebook's published 0.15% follower-based default because total follower count isn't in the export [[Engagement rate vs. benchmark|chart-benchmark]].
analysis_paragraphs: The headline story in August is a reach contraction, not an engagement problem. Views and reach both dropped 7.9% per day versus July [[Performance table|perf-table]], but the views-per-reach ratio was essentially identical across all three months (~1.4286 in June, July, and August — [[Views & reach trend|chart-views-reach]]), meaning each person reached saw the same number of views each time. Fewer people were reached; the content shown to them performed the same or slightly better.

Interactions fell far less than views (-1.3%/day vs. -7.9%/day — [[Interactions & link clicks trend|chart-int-clicks]]), so the reach-based engagement rate actually rose to 1.96% in August from 1.83% in July and June (+0.13pt). Because the export doesn't include a total-follower count, this rate can only be benchmarked on a reach basis, and Facebook's commonly cited 0.15% default is follower-based — nearly 13x lower by methodology alone, not performance — so no over/under-performance claim is made here [[Engagement rate vs. benchmark|chart-benchmark]].

On follower growth, net new followers fell 1.6%/day from July to August. Decomposing the change: gross follows per day dropped from 179.97 to 177.74 (-2.23/day), which more than fully explains the net decline; unfollows per day also eased slightly, from 58.39 to 58.13 (-0.26/day), which cushioned the net decline by about 13%. In short, softer top-of-funnel discovery, not a retention problem, is driving the slower follower growth [[Performance table|perf-table]].

At the content level, August's segment data (supplied for August only, so no month-over-month segment comparison is possible) shows Reels converting views to revenue roughly 1.6x as efficiently as Photos (Reels: 44% of revenue from 33% of views; Photos: 47% of revenue from 50% of views) [[Segment breakdown|segment-table]], [[Revenue by segment|chart-segment-rev]]. Text and Live remain minor contributors at 5% and 4% of revenue respectively.

A single day, August 16, posted 9,106 interactions against a monthly daily average of 5,484 (+66%) and 508,993 views, the month's highest. That one day contributed 5.4% of August's total interactions [[Daily interactions|chart-daily-int]]. August 8, by contrast, was the softest day at 3,365 interactions (-39% vs. average).

recommendations.title: Shift incremental content investment toward Reels
recommendations.body: Reels converts views to revenue at roughly 1.6x the rate of Photos (44% of revenue from 33% of views vs. Photos' 47% from 50%). Increasing Reels' share of the content mix is the fastest lever to grow revenue without needing more total reach [[Segment breakdown|segment-table]].

recommendations.title: Reverse-engineer the August 16 spike
recommendations.body: August 16 generated 66% more interactions than an average August day and was the single-largest contributor (5.4%) to the month's interaction total. Identify what was posted that day and test whether the format or topic is repeatable [[Daily interactions|chart-daily-int]].

recommendations.title: Investigate the reach decline before assuming a content problem
recommendations.body: Views and reach fell together while views-per-reach stayed flat at ~1.43 across all three months, so this is a distribution/reach issue (algorithmic or posting-frequency related), not declining content quality — engagement on the content that was shown actually improved [[Views & reach trend|chart-views-reach]].

recommendations.title: Diagnose the softer gross-follow rate
recommendations.body: The net follower slowdown (3,708 vs. 3,769, -1.6%/day) is fully explained by fewer gross follows (-2.23/day), not by rising unfollows, which actually eased slightly. Treat this as a top-of-funnel/discovery question rather than a retention one [[Performance table|perf-table]].

recommendations.title: Request Impressions and total-follower-count fields in future exports
recommendations.body: CTR (link clicks / impressions) is Unavailable this month because no export included an Impressions column, and engagement rate could only be computed on a reach basis because total follower count wasn't present either — both are needed for benchmarkable, like-for-like comparisons going forward [[Performance table|perf-table]].

benchmark_sources.source: Quid/Rival IQ 2026 Social Media Industry Benchmark Report

data_notes: No account/page name was present in any supplied export; "Page" is used as a placeholder label in this report.

Three daily exports were supplied: facebook_export_2026-06.csv (30 days), facebook_export_2026-07.csv (31 days), facebook_export_2026-08.csv (31 days), plus facebook_segments_2026-08.csv (content-segment breakdown for August only).
The August daily export did not include a Visits column (present in June and July); Visits is marked Unavailable for August rather than estimated.
No export included an Impressions column, so CTR (link clicks ÷ impressions) is Unavailable for all three months.

No export included a total page-follower count, so engagement rate is computed on reach (unique viewers) rather than followers; it is shown against the Facebook benchmark with denominators labeled, and no over/under-performance verdict is given due to the mismatch.
Segment-level data (Photos/Reels/Text/Live) was supplied only for August; no June or July segment files were provided, so a month-over-month segment comparison could not be made.

Segment totals reconcile against the daily August export within rounding: segment Views sum to 12,401,579 vs. 12,401,581 from the daily file; segment Interactions sum to 170,002 vs. 170,003 from the daily file (differences of 2 and 1, consistent with per-post rounding in the segment export).
No ad-spend data was supplied, so ROI/cost-per-X metrics are not included.
